builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HBQ: Hierarchical Scaling Block Quantization with Hardware-Efficiency-Aware Design for Accurate LLM Inference
summary: HBQ replaces small-block PoT/integer-scaled block quantization and weight-only quantization with large-block W4A5 quantization plus a second-level significand scale, implemented on a custom 28nm ASIC datapath covering weights, activations, and KV cache. The cost is that the claimed efficiency depends on purpose-built silicon and a unified low-precision datapath; there is no GPU kernel or software path reported, so the gains do not transfer to a 24 GB GPU or API-based deployment. It can fail for the reader because large blocks inherently degrade accuracy unless the SIG scaling generalizes across models, and without the custom hardware the method reduces to a quantization format with no supported runtime.
rationale: The benefits are demonstrated only on custom ASIC hardware, so an engineer limited to a single GPU or third-party APIs cannot realize them and should track the work rather than adopt it.
technique: Hierarchical Block Quantization with significand scaling

claims.statement: HBQ replaces small-block PoT/integer-scaled block quantization and weight-only quantization with large-block W4A5 quantization plus a second-level significand scale, implemented on a custom 28nm ASIC datapath covering weights, activations, and KV cache. The cost is that the claimed efficiency depends on purpose-built silicon and a unified low-precision datapath; there is no GPU kernel or software path reported, so the gains do not transfer to a 24 GB GPU or API-based deployment. It can fail for the reader because large blocks inherently degrade accuracy unless the SIG scaling generalizes across models, and without the custom hardware the method reduces to a quantization format with no supported runtime.

ASIC results report 2.3x/4.6x higher area/energy efficiency than state-of-the-art weight-only quantization at equal accuracy, 1.6-3.3x system energy reduction and 1.5-3.0x speedup over prior block quantization methods, with W4A5 achieving W4A16-level accuracy.
